description: Key Hansard speeches from C-14 (2016) and C-7 (2020-2021) MAID debates. These are the words MPs used to justify expanding state-sanctioned killing.

key_speeches.speaker: Jody Wilson-Raybould
key_speeches.role: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
key_quotes: Bill C-14 represents the government's policy choice to address medical assistance in dying, a choice that is fully informed by consultations with Canadians and experts.

An assisted death could be an acceptable treatment for a soldier with post-traumatic stress disorder, a young person who suffered a spinal cord injury in an accident, or a survivor whose mind was haunted by memories of sexual abuse.
Under an approach where any serious medical condition is eligible, the law would be saying that an assisted death could be an acceptable treatment for a soldier with post-traumatic stress disorder.
The eligibility criterion requiring a reasonably foreseeable natural death would be repealed.
While the Carter decision told us that an absolute prohibition in the former law went too far, it did not tell us how medical assistance in dying should be implemented.
I call on all members of the House to support Bill C-14.
key_speeches.context: Wilson-Raybould moved third reading. Despite warning about risks to vulnerable people including PTSD soldiers and abuse survivors, she championed the bill that opened the door to MAID expansion. She was later fired from cabinet by Trudeau during the SNC-Lavalin affair.

key_speeches.speaker: Cathy McLeod
key_quotes: I heard this from 100% of the people in my riding, is that there should be very clear and specific language on the protection of the health conscience rights of our health care providers.
Last night, we turned down what I thought was a very reasoned amendment.
key_speeches.context: McLeod challenged the government's rejection of conscience protection amendments for healthcare workers. The Liberals voted against protecting doctors who refused to participate in MAID.

key_speeches.speaker: Mark Warawa
key_quotes: 84% of Canadians do support this under certain criteria, and that criteria is that the illness is terminal, and the person is suffering terribly and repeatedly asks to have assisted suicide to end their suffering.
70% of physicians in Canada do not want to be a part of this. They do not want to be forced through coercion, intimidation, or threats.
A young medical student asked me if physicians were going to be forced to do this and I said that there is a good possibility.
Physicians across this country are going to refuse to participate, saying they are now of retirement age and will retire or will relocate to another jurisdiction.
A shortage of physicians and nurses will create a medical emergency in Canada.
key_speeches.context: Warawa exposed that the government refused ALL Conservative amendments including conscience protection. He warned of a physician exodus — a prediction confirmed by subsequent reports of doctors leaving practice.
key_speeches.note: Mark Warawa died in 2019. His warnings about physician coercion proved prophetic.

key_speeches.speaker: John Barlow
key_quotes: There is no funding in the 2016 budget for palliative care. We tried to put an amendment through last night, which was voted down.
What is the long-term plan for palliative care?
key_speeches.context: Barlow exposed that the government was pushing MAID without funding palliative care — forcing people toward death rather than comfort. This remains true: Canada still has grossly inadequate palliative care coverage in 2026.

key_facts.note: Government used time allocation to limit debate. Only 3 NDP members got to speak at third reading.

votes_on_amendments.description: Require palliative care consultation before MAID request
Require consultation for underlying mental health condition
Require psychiatric examination for underlying mental health
Require judicial oversight of MAID requests
Refer back to committee re: Carter consistency

key_speeches.speaker: Arif Virani
key_speeches.role: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice
key_quotes: I am really disappointed, to be frank, to see my colleagues across the aisle delaying the bill, increasing the chances that the government misses the court-imposed deadline and prolongs the suffering of Canadians.
We know that the majority of Canadians believe that MAID is a basic human right.
The eligibility criterion requiring a reasonably foreseeable natural death would be repealed.
I am very disheartened to see members of the Conservative Party of Canada continue their delay tactics to slow this legislation.
Prolonging the suffering of Canadians is not in any of our interests and that is exactly what will transpire if the December 18 deadline is missed.
This period of 90 days is not a waiting period or a reflection period.
key_speeches.context: Virani framed opposition as 'prolonging suffering' — weaponizing compassion to silence debate on expanding MAID to people whose death was NOT foreseeable. He dismissed disability organizations' concerns as not representative. The bill removed the 'foreseeable death' requirement, opening MAID to chronically ill and disabled Canadians.

key_speeches.speaker: Maryam Monsef
key_quotes: moved that Bill C-7, An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying), be read the third time and passed.
key_speeches.context: Monsef moved third reading of C-7. She also voted for C-14.

key_speeches.speaker: Rob Moore
key_quotes: Not one of the amendments that were proposed by our Conservative Party at committee was adopted.
Krista Carr, executive vice-president of Inclusion Canada, a group that represents persons with disabilities, said that Bill C-7 represents the 'worst nightmare' for persons with disabilities.

Why did they not listen to the persons with disabilities community and why is he talking about delays, when it was his government that prorogued the House and caused Bill C-7 to have to have a complete restart.
key_speeches.context: Moore exposed that the government rejected ALL Conservative amendments and ignored disability organizations. Inclusion Canada called C-7 the 'worst nightmare' for disabled Canadians.

key_speeches.speaker: Garnett Genuis
key_quotes: When all of the representative organizations who represent people with disabilities are raising big concerns, I think the government should take that seriously.
The Conservatives wanted the House to be able to sit in May and June. The Liberal government chose not to allow the House to sit.
key_speeches.context: Genuis challenged the government for cherry-picking disability voices and pointed out the Liberals deliberately prevented Parliament from sitting during COVID to avoid debate.

key_speeches.speaker: Gérard Deltell
key_quotes: Since this issue is literally about life or death, would it not have been better to have the Supreme Court of Canada as the court to rule definitively on this issue?
key_speeches.context: Deltell questioned why the government chose not to appeal the Truchon decision to the Supreme Court, instead using a lower court ruling to justify expanding MAID nationwide.

key_speeches.speaker: Randall Garrison
key_quotes: COVID was partially responsible for the delay, but certainly the Liberal government's prorogation was a bigger cause for the delay.
What are the consequences for Quebec and for the rest of the country if we do not meet this deadline?
key_speeches.context: NDP acknowledged Liberal prorogation caused the delay, yet still supported the bill. The NDP provided critical support to pass C-7.

key_speeches.speaker: Luc Thériault
key_quotes: Does she believe it is acceptable and humane for a person to have to go on a hunger strike to be able to access medical assistance in dying?
key_speeches.context: Thériault pushed for broader access, arguing C-14 was too restrictive. The Bloc consistently pushed for the widest possible MAID access throughout both C-14 and C-7 debates.

key_facts.what_changed: Removed 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' requirement — opened MAID to chronically ill and disabled people NOT dying
key_facts.independent_witness: No longer required to be independent — paid caregivers qualify
key_facts.mental_illness_exclusion: Temporary — sunset clause set for March 2023, extended to March 2024, then March 2027
key_facts.disability_quote: Bill C-7 represents the 'worst nightmare' for persons with disabilities — Krista Carr, Inclusion Canada
key_facts.prorogation: Liberals prorogued Parliament Aug 2020 (WE Charity scandal), causing C-7 restart and rushed timeline
key_facts.court_deadline_manufactured: Government chose NOT to appeal Truchon to SCC — manufactured own deadline
key_facts.closure_motion: March 11, 2021 — closure used on Senate amendments vote

senate_amendments_controversy.description: Senate added sunset clause for mental illness exclusion — government accepted, opening path to MAID for mental illness
senate_amendments_controversy.original_bill: Excluded mental illness as sole underlying condition permanently
senate_amendments_controversy.senate_amendment: Added sunset clause — mental illness exclusion expires after 2 years
senate_amendments_controversy.government_response: ACCEPTED the sunset clause — agreed to open MAID to mental illness cases

votes.description: Amendment to reject mental illness sunset
Accept Senate amendments including mental illness sunset

Rejected ALL opposition amendments on both C-14 and C-7
Manufactured court deadlines by refusing to appeal (C-14: Carter June 6 deadline; C-7: Truchon Dec 18 deadline)
Prorogued Parliament during WE scandal, then claimed urgency to rush C-7
Weaponized compassion — framed opposition as 'prolonging suffering'
Dismissed disability organizations as not representative of all disabled people
Cherry-picked individual disabled voices who supported MAID while ignoring representative organizations
safeguards_removed_or_never_added: Conscience protection for healthcare workers — REJECTED
Judicial oversight of MAID requests — REJECTED
Two independent witnesses — REDUCED to one, no independence required
Foreseeable death requirement — REMOVED by C-7
Mental illness exclusion — SUNSET CLAUSE added, expiring 2027
predictions_that_came_true: Mark Warawa (2016): Predicted physician exodus — confirmed by CMA workforce reports
John Barlow (2016): Warned no palliative care funding — Canada still lacks universal palliative care in 2026
Rob Moore (2020): Warned disability community opposed — MAID deaths among non-terminal disabled people surged
Multiple MPs (2016): Warned about slippery slope — C-7 removed foreseeable death requirement 4 years later
Conservatives (2016): Warned about conscience rights — Ontario and other provinces forced effective referral
